sonnet.problem: Card 1 already says 'the prince of Greece will come' (Daniel 10:20), so it gives away the answer 'Greece' to this later fill-in-the-blank. The wrong answers Egypt and Assyria are also easy to rule out because of it.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The True statement says the king of the North 'will be stopped by a commander.' Verse 18 says only that a commander 'will put an end to his reproach and will turn it back upon him.' The card turns that into 'stopped,' which stretches the text.
sonnet.rule: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess a word in a line they haven't been told: 'the holy ___' with covenant, prophets or scrolls. No story card sets up verse 28 and nothing lets the baker reason to 'covenant,' so the card tests wording, not meaning.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The blank 'abolish the daily ___' (sacrifice, prayers or psalms) asks the baker to guess a wording from verse 31. No story card gives the context, so a reasoned pick isn't possible.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
